delete.description: Archives the institution: it leaves pickers and stays on the accounts that use it.

get.description: The user's accounts by name, each with its balance, the total balance of each institution in each currency, and the totals of each institution and of everything in the user's base currency, at today's exchange rates. A balance with no rate to convert it is left out of those and listed as not converted. The totals cover the whole list, whichever page is asked for. Archived accounts, which pickers never offer, only with includeArchived=true.

post.description: Adds an account. A credit card or loan sends amountOwed, a positive number, and shows a negative balance; any other type sends openingBalance. Any account can be labelled with the last 4 digits of its number, never more of it. Only a credit card takes creditLimit, statementDay and paymentDueDay.

get.description: One account, archived or not, with its balance. The ETag header carries its row version.

put.description: Changes an account; its balance follows a new opening balance at once, and a credit card's available credit a new credit limit. Every field is replaced: last4 or a credit card field left out is removed. Send the row version last read as If-Match: a stale one answers 412, none answers 428.

delete.description: Archives the account, at any balance: it leaves lists and pickers and stays in history.

get.description: The user's categories as a tree: top-level categories, each with its subcategories. Archived ones, which pickers never offer, only with includeArchived=true.

post.description: Adds a top-level category, or a subcategory when parentId is set. A subcategory has its parent's kind; categories are at most two levels deep.

put.description: Renames, recolours or re-icons a category, or changes a top-level category's kind together with its subcategories. The kind cannot change once any of them has transactions.

delete.description: Archives the category and its subcategories: they leave pickers and stay on the transactions that use them.

get.description: The user's transactions that pass every filter sent, a page at a time, with the total of all that pass, whichever page is asked for. Newest date first and, within a date, last recorded first, unless sort and order say otherwise. A deleted transaction is never listed or counted. The two legs of a transfer are listed like any transaction, each on its own account, with the transferId they share; the total counts them and adds them to neither income nor expenses.

post.description: Records income or an expense on an account, in the account's currency; the account's balance follows at once. An expense flagged isRefund is a refund and raises the balance. Send lines in place of categoryId to split it across categories: lines that do not sum exactly to the amount are refused. Send an Idempotency-Key the client made up for this transaction: a retry with the same key answers the transaction the first request recorded and records nothing, and a different transaction sent with a key already used answers 422.

get.description: What quick add starts a new transaction from: the account, not archived, that the user recorded a transaction on last, and the category, not archived, they most often gave the payee. Send the payee as typed; it suggests a category once it is, in any case, a payee the user has used before.

The user's recently deleted transactions: those deleted in the last 30 days, which can still be restored, the last deleted first, a page at a time. Each leg of a deleted transfer is listed. After 30 days a deleted transaction is no longer listed or restorable, and the worker removes it for good.

post.description: Restores a transaction deleted in the last 30 days: it is back in lists and its account's balance at once, as it was when it was deleted. Restoring a leg of a transfer restores the whole transfer, the other leg with it. One that is not deleted, or was deleted longer ago, is not found. The ETag header carries its row version.

get.description: One transaction. The ETag header carries its row version. A deleted transaction is not found.

put.description: Changes income or an expense; the balance of its account, and of the account it was moved from, follows at once. Send the row version last read as If-Match: a stale one answers 412, none answers 428. A leg of a transfer is refused on its type: edit the transfer under /transfers. A reconciled transaction refuses a change to its amount, date, account, type or refund flag, each named as the field at fault; its payee, note and category can still change.

delete.description: Deletes the transaction: it leaves lists and its account's balance at once. Deleting a leg of a transfer deletes the whole transfer, the other leg with it. A reconciled transaction, or a leg of a transfer either of whose legs is reconciled, answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:transaction-reconciled and is not deleted.

get.description: The user's tags by name, a page at a time: what the transaction form suggests as a tag is typed. A tag is created the first time a transaction is given it.

post.description: Moves money between two of the user's accounts. It records two linked transactions, a transferOut leg on the source account and a transferIn leg on the destination, and both balances follow at once; a transfer is neither income nor spending. Between accounts in different currencies send both amounts: no exchange rate is looked up. Send an Idempotency-Key the client made up for this transfer: a retry with the same key answers the transfer the first request recorded and records nothing, and anything else sent with a key already used answers 422. A retry after the transfer was unmarked answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:transfer-unmarked and records nothing: a new transfer needs a new key.

get.description: One transfer, by the transferId its two legs carry in the transaction list. The ETag header carries its row version. A deleted transfer is not found.

put.description: Changes a transfer, both legs together; the balances of the accounts it was and is now between follow at once. Send the row version last read as If-Match: a stale one answers 412, none answers 428. A transfer either of whose legs is reconciled refuses a change to its accounts, amounts or date, each named as the field at fault; its note can still change.

delete.description: Deletes the transfer, both legs together: they leave the transaction list and both accounts' balances at once. A transfer either of whose legs is reconciled answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:transaction-reconciled and is not deleted.

post.description: Marks an expense on one account and income on another as one transfer, such as the two rows imported statements show for paying a card: the expense becomes its transferOut leg and the income its transferIn leg, each keeping its id, account, amount, date and note and losing its category and payee, so neither counts as spending or income any more. The two must be on different accounts, on the same date and, between accounts in one currency, of the same amount; an expense that is a refund, a transaction that is a leg of a transfer already, or a reconciled one, is refused. Nothing is matched automatically.

Turns a transfer back into two ordinary transactions: its transferOut leg becomes an expense on expenseCategoryId and its transferIn leg income on incomeCategoryId, each keeping its id, account, amount, date and note. Any transfer can be unmarked, marked or recorded, unless either leg is reconciled: that is refused on id. Answers the two transactions; the transfer is no more.

Starts reconciling the account against a statement: its closing date, not in the future, and closing balance, in the account's currency and below zero for what is owed. The difference starts as the statement balance less the account's reconciled balance: its opening balance and everything reconciled before. An account has one reconciliation in progress at a time: another answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:reconciliation-in-progress. A statement dated before the account's last reconciliation is refused on statementDate.

get.description: The account's reconciliations, the last started first, a page at a time, each with its difference.
One reconciliation, with the account's reconciled balance, what is ticked in it and the difference still to reach zero.

delete.description: Cancels a reconciliation in progress, entered against the wrong statement for instance: what is ticked in it is unticked and it is removed. A completed one answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:reconciliation-completed: reopen it first.

get.description: The transactions to tick against the statement, oldest first: those ticked in this reconciliation and, while it is in progress, every other transaction on its account dated on or before the statement date that no reconciliation holds yet. Not paged.

put.description: Ticks a transaction the statement shows, and answers the reconciliation with its new difference. Only a transaction on the account, dated on or before the statement date and in no other reconciliation can be ticked; any other is refused on transactionId. A completed reconciliation answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:reconciliation-completed.

delete.description: Unticks a transaction, and answers the reconciliation with its new difference. A completed reconciliation answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:reconciliation-completed.

post.description: Completes the reconciliation, which locks every transaction ticked in it: their amount, date and account cannot change, and they cannot be deleted, until it is reopened. It completes only when the difference is exactly zero; otherwise it answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:reconciliation-difference-not-zero, and no adjustment transaction is ever added. Completing one already completed changes nothing.

Reopens a completed reconciliation: its transactions are unlocked and stay ticked, to be changed and completed again. Only the account's latest reconciliation can be reopened; an earlier one answers 409 with the problem type urn:pfm:problem:reconciliation-not-latest. Reopening one in progress changes nothing.

get.description: The receipts attached to a transaction, the first attached first.

post.description: Attaches a receipt to a transaction: one JPEG, PNG or PDF file of at most 5 MB, sent as the file field of a multipart/form-data body. What the file is, is read from the file itself, not from its name.

get.description: A signed URL that opens the attached file. It works for a few minutes and needs no sign-in, so ask for it when the user opens the file, and never keep it.

delete.description: Removes the attachment from its transaction and deletes its file.

get.description: The user's recurring rules, the last set up first.

post.description: Sets up income or an expense that repeats. The worker posts each occurrence as a transaction on its due date, in the user's time zone. A start date in the past is allowed: the occurrences since then are posted, each on its own due date.

get.description: Every occurrence of the user's recurring rules due after today, in their time zone, and within the days asked for, earliest first: the ones the worker will post and the ones that will be reminders. A paused rule has none.
The user's reminders, earliest due first: each occurrence of a rule that reminds, due on or before today in their time zone, not yet confirmed or dismissed. A paused rule has none.
One recurring rule. The ETag header carries its row version.

put.description: Replaces what the rule's next transactions say and when they are due. Transactions it already posted stay as they are, and a new schedule carries on after the last occurrence posted or skipped. Send the row version last read as If-Match: a stale one answers 412, none answers 428. Posting an occurrence, pausing and resuming change the row version too.

delete.description: Deletes the rule: it posts nothing more. The transactions it posted stay, no longer linked to a rule.

post.description: Pauses the rule: it posts nothing until it is resumed.
Resumes a paused rule: it posts again from today. The occurrences that were due while it was paused are skipped.

Confirms a reminder: its transaction is recorded, dated on its due date, saying what the rule says, for the amount sent or else the rule's own, and the rule moves on to its next occurrence. A rule's reminders are confirmed or dismissed earliest first: a later one answers 400 on dueDate. Confirming one twice records one transaction.
Dismisses a reminder: nothing is recorded for it, and the rule moves on to its next occurrence. A rule's reminders are confirmed or dismissed earliest first: a later one answers 400 on dueDate.

get.description: The budgets of one budget month (a calendar month from the 1st), in the user's base currency: budgeted, spent, remaining and state for each, with totals. Spent is worked out from the month's expenses every time, each as converted at the exchange rate of its own date; an expense in a subcategory counts toward a budget on its parent, and transfers and income never count. Without month, the month it is now in the user's time zone.

put.description: Sets the budget of an expense category for a month, in the user's base currency, which is locked from the first budget on. A category and its subcategory cannot both have a budget in the same month. Setting a new budget answers 201 and sends no If-Match; changing the amount of one that exists answers 200 and must send the row version last read as If-Match: a stale one answers 412, none answers 428.

delete.description: Removes the budget a category has in a month.

post.description: Copies the budgets of the source month into the month in one action, such as last month's into this one, each with its amount.

get.description: Where the money went over a period: what the expenses in each category came to, minus refunds, with each one's share of the total, in the user's base currency and ranked, most first. Each expense counts as converted at the exchange rate of its own date; one that is not converted is left out and counted in notConverted. Transfers and income never count, and each line of a split counts in its own category. Without parentId each top-level category stands for itself and its subcategories; with it, each of that category's subcategories stands for itself, and the category for what was spent on it directly.

The last step of drilling down spending by category: the expenses with a line on one category itself (not on its subcategories) over a period, newest first, each with what it spent there in the base currency, so they add up to that category's spent in the report. A split shows only its lines on the category; a refund spends a negative amount; one that is not converted spends nothing yet and is counted in notConverted. Not paged: one category's expenses over one period.

Am I within budget: each category's budgets against what was spent against them, in the user's base currency, over the whole budget months the period touches (one month, or several summed). A budget counts what was spent in its own month, in its category and, for a top-level one, in its subcategories, as on the budget screen; the account filter narrows what counts as spent, never the budgets. What was spent in a month where no budget covered its category is listed apart under unbudgeted. An expense that is not converted is left out of spent and counted in notConverted. Not compared with the previous period.

One category or one payee over time: what it came to in each month of a period, in the user's base currency, and how each month changed from the one before, as an amount and a percentage. A category with its subcategories adds up spent (its expenses minus refunds) when it is an expense category, and the income received in it when it is an income one; a payee adds up what was spent with it, or with type income the income received from it, matched in any case, and with categoryId too only in that category. Each transaction counts as converted at the exchange rate of its own date; one that is not converted is left out and counted in notConverted. Transfers never count. With compare, the period before is worked out the same way, and change says how the total moved from it.

Am I saving: income, expenses and net in each calendar month of a period, with the savings rate, and the same over the whole period, in the user's base currency. Expenses are spent: refunds lower them. Net is income minus expenses; the savings rate is net as a percentage of income, to one decimal, and none when income is not above zero. Each transaction counts as converted at the exchange rate of its own date; one that is not converted is left out and counted in notConverted. Transfers are neither income nor expenses and never count. With categoryId, only the lines in that category and its subcategories count.

What the user is worth over a period: at each month end in it, and on its last day when it ends inside a month, the balances of the assets (every account but credit cards and loans) and the amount owed on the liabilities (credit cards and loans), and the assets minus the liabilities, in the user's base currency. Archived accounts count; an account counts from its opening date. Each balance is converted at the exchange rate of the day it is shown on, or the nearest earlier one; one with no rate on or before that day is left out and counted in notConverted. Not paged: one item per month.

A one-document summary of a calendar month, as a PDF file to download: its income, expenses, net and savings rate, spending by top-level category with each one's share, and each budget against what was spent, with what was spent where no budget covered it, all in the user's base currency, worked out as the income vs expenses, spending by category and budget vs actual reports work them out for that month. Written in the locale asked for, or the user's own, or English when they have none, with amounts written the locale's way.
